additional_info.body:
Dear Ramona,
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Shrey
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center - ERK
Main Asset
:
MP / R6 170002073
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
q5xSLu
Problem Description
: DC4 out of order
Troubleshooting
: We have analyzed the logs and found that the charger is operating in fail-safe mode due to the dispenser PLC not being in an operational state. Please coordinate with the site intervention to physically check that the dispenser PLC is in the RUN state. Ensure that the Ethernet connections to both the dispenser PLC and the charger are secure and that there are no loose connections. Additionally, verify that all connections to the dispenser LEM of the DC4 outlet are properly connected. If possible, bring a spare LEM and dispenser PLC in advance, if these components cannot be replaced, they can be procured at another site in the future. We tried rebooting the charger but it didn't help it out.

additional_info.body:
Hi Sascha,
Greetings of the day!
To provide a better understanding of the issue, the ticket was initially created when the charger was in Fail Safe mode, and basic preliminary troubleshooting steps were shared on the same day. The following day, you requested the MLFB or device tags, which you emailed in the ticket. However, since the ticket is in your queue, we did not receive notifications about it.
As mentioned in your previous communication, the Fail Safe issue in the charger was resolved, and now the fuse in the dispenser is tripped. We recommend that you order the spare parts and proceed with the necessary replacement activity.
Please ensure that if you need any assistance during the intervention, you reach out to the NOC team so that someone from our team can provide support.
MLFB :
5SK9106-1
( -FC212, -FC213, -FC214 )
Description : Electronic Device Protection 1P 6A 24VDC
Regarding the blown fuse, please ensure that there are no loose connections or short circuits within the charger or at the connections going through the fuses.
Check wiring for potential short-circuit or overload of 24V supply
Check wiring for trip line interlock from Sicharge-d to dispenser along with 24V voltage at various points in trip line at dispenser side, when door limit switch has been temporarily defeated
Handing over the case back to your queue as field service is required to check for any loose connections or short circuits within the dispenser and to replace the fuse that was tripped.
